tasks.title: Gimbal pitch servo pulse
tasks.solution: move_servo: v = (θ − MIN) / (MAX − MIN), constrained to 0…1; with REVERSED = 1 take 1 − v; PWM = SERVOn_MIN + ⌊v · (SERVOn_MAX − SERVOn_MIN)⌋. SERVOn_TRIM takes no part. An angle outside the limits gives the end pulse. The module example: −90…20, 1100…1900, 0° → 1754 µs, −45° → 1427 µs.

tasks.title: Trigger distance and number of pictures on a line
tasks.solution: The spacing is d = footprint · (1 − overlap). The first position after the command is only stored, and a picture is taken every d meters. The check runs 50 times a second, so the actual spacing is slightly more than d, and a picture that would fall exactly on the end of the line is already past it: N = ⌈L / d⌉ − 1 (if L is not a multiple of d, this is the same as ⌊L / d⌋). With p3 = 1 a picture at the start would be added. The module example: 120 · 0.2 = 24 m, 610 / 24 → 25 pictures; a 600 m line would give 24.

tasks.title: Actual spacing in a tailwind
tasks.solution: If d / v ≥ T, the picture is taken by distance and the spacing is d. Otherwise the trigger waits for CAM1_INTRVAL_MIN, the vehicle does not slow down, and the spacing is v · T. The result is max(d, v · T). The module example: 24 m, 1.5 s, 18 m/s → 27 m. The check once every 20 ms adds up to v · 0.02 m more, which is neglected here.

tasks.title: Georeferencing error without shutter feedback
tasks.solution: Without the pin a CAM record is the moment of the command; the shutter fires v · τ farther along the track. On opposite lines the errors point in opposite directions: the mutual shift is 2 · v · τ. The module example: 12 m/s, 0.12 s → 1.44 m per picture, 2.88 m between lines.

tasks.title: Release lead distance (no air drag)
tasks.solution: The fall time is t = √(2h / g), and the payload keeps its horizontal speed: x = v · t. Assumptions: a point payload, no drag and no wind, level ground. A real payload lands closer. The module example: 30 m and 10 m/s → 2.47 s, 24.7 m.
